title: Marguerite and the Wreck
premise: Desert ranger Casper Blackwood is chasing a thief named Marguerite Voss across the Redline Range when a government survey team vanishes without tracks, leaving their gear neatly stacked and their radio still warm. Forced into an uneasy alliance, Casper and Marguerite discover the surveyors were mapping a glacier route the government intends to seal — and weaponize — before calving season opens it for six days. Racing the snows with two surviving surveyors who have become their found family, they must decide whether duty means delivering the maps or destroying them. In the end, Casper lets Marguerite burn the survey, chooses her over the badge he's worn for fifteen years, and the four of them cross the range as the ice closes behind them, free and officially dead.
about_author: C. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former backcountry ranger turned novelist who writes adventure fiction from a cabin at the edge of a fire-scarred forest. Their work is known for austere landscapes, morally tangled loyalties, and characters who find family in the worst places on earth.

chapters.title: Nothing Forgives
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Tracking a thief through the high desert, Casper reflects on fifteen years of service and the wilderness that has cost him everything but his badge. He corners the thief at a dry wash — and finds she's been leaving water caches for someone else. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Left Water
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Marguerite Voss reveals she stole government documents to expose a sealed glacier route, and that her brother was one of the vanished surveyors. Casper should arrest her; instead he follows her to the abandoned survey camp. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the camp they find equipment stacked with military precision, no footprints, and a radio transmitting coordinates into empty air. Two survivors emerge from a snow cave: surveyor Idris Okafor and medic Sana Reyes. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Six Days
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Idris explains the glacier calving season opens the pass for six days — and that the survey data would let the government collapse the route permanently and control all northern passage. The group votes to carry the evidence out themselves. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The climb begins; a storm erases the trail and Sana nearly dies in a crevasse Casper anchors them out of by hand. A government recovery helicopter passes overhead and does not stop. Emotional beat: the first fracture in Casper's faith in duty.

chapters.title: What the Badge Is For
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Sheltering in a derelict fire lookout, Marguerite and Casper argue about law versus justice while Idris decrypts the survey files and learns the mission was never scientific. Casper admits he was sent to retrieve the data, not rescue anyone. Emotional beat: betrayal, then forgiveness chosen anyway.

chapters.title: The Calving Fields
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They reach the ice fields as the season opens, crossing beneath groaning seracs while a government retrieval team shadows them. Sana is injured covering the group's escape from an ambush. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Cornered at the far lip of the glacier, Marguerite holds the only copy of the survey and the chance to clear her name if she surrenders it. She hesitates — not for herself, but because burning it erases her brother's last work. Emotional beat: grief weighed against principle.

chapters.title: The Ice Gives Way
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax: the glacier calves early, splitting the party from the retrieval team. Casper burns the survey himself, takes the blame, and holds the collapsing route open while the others cross. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided in ten seconds of falling ice.

chapters.title: Officially Dead
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. On the far side, the four bury the badges, the files, and their old names under the snowmelt. News reports list the survey team lost; no one is looking for a ranger or a thief. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace — a family made in the wreck of everything else.
